messages.author: c9541177104aea27
messages.subject: rhipe and hadoop fair scheduler
parts:
Hi,

I have a CDH3 env implemented with fair-schelduling, everything works fine until
I have the scenario whereby an application is running which currently has been allocated
all the resources available on the cluster. Under normal circumstances, the next job submitted
will then work to get its fair share of resources and it too, will start to run with the fair scheduler
properly allocating the resources.

For rhipe, if I submit the job and it is the first job to ask for the resources, the job will run without
any issues, even if another job comes in and starts to get its fair share of resources, the jobs will
run just fine (I've had up to 8 running, each with the fair share of resources)

If there is another job already using the resources and I start up an R job it will fail to start and will
not attempt to run, generating failed statuses for each task.

It seems as long as rhipe can get its request and not get queued up, that everything is fine, but as
soon as it needs to compete for the resources it will not start or queue.

Am I missing a rhipe configuration parameter, I looked through all the basic ones, but did not
find one that would address this.

thanks,

Jim

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] rhipe and hadoop fair scheduler
parts:
RHIPE is really Hadoop Streaming very customized. I see the issue is during the
Reduce phase. I don't think there is a RHIPE option for this per se, rather some
Hadoop option. We regularly have 10-15 jobs running on our cluster and i don't
see these errors.

keep in mind, RHIPE launches an R process for every task (it would be possible
to launch once per JVM, but it's tricky to find out when the JVM shuts down)

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.author: c9541177104aea27
messages.subject: Re: rhipe and hadoop fair scheduler
parts:
Hi,

I'm not sure about the reduce phase, I am testing this with an R job that only
maps. This particular issue didn't start occurring until the fair-scheduler was
introduced, no other applications that run M/R have any issues, and it is only
if an application is running that currently owns the resources and the scheduler
needs to re-allocate them to rhipe that rhipe gets upset and generates the
errors. If the rhipe job is running already, it will give up the resources it owns
to the FS (there are some high priority jobs that must run and are very aggressive
at getting their resources), but the rhipe job will continue on and complete without any
issues, even rescheduling those tasks that were killed by the high priority jobs and
completing those as well.

My first thought is that rhipe is not waiting until the resources are free, the wait time
I have set is 180s before rhipe can get aggressive and demand the resources.

I will look at the FS and streaming jobs more closely.

Jim
